rationales: Observations are gathered using the senses or instruments, not the main point at which reasoning is used.
Reasoning may help form a hypothesis, but the question most directly refers to using reasoning to make deductions.
A biologist uses reasoning to draw deductions from a hypothesis or evidence.
Organizing data arranges results; it is not the best answer for when reasoning is used.
Family is a higher taxonomic rank and is not the first name in binomial nomenclature.
Class is a higher taxonomic rank and is not the first name in binomial nomenclature.
Species is the second part of a binomial name, not the first.
The first name in binomial nomenclature identifies the genus.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831.
1832 is not the year of Brown’s discovery of the nucleus.
1833 is not the year of Brown’s discovery of the nucleus.
1834 is not the year of Brown’s discovery of the nucleus.
Adipose tissue is not epithelial tissue; it stores fat and supports the body.
Adipose tissue is a type of connective tissue.
Adipose tissue is not muscle tissue, which contracts to produce movement.
Adipose tissue is not nervous tissue, which transmits nerve impulses.
Mitochondria do not divide during karyokinesis.
Cytoplasm divides during cytokinesis, not karyokinesis.
Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
The cell membrane does not divide as part of karyokinesis.
Insulin is a hormone, not the protein forming spindle microtubules.
Myosin is a motor protein involved in muscle contraction, not the main spindle microtubule protein.
Actin forms microfilaments and is not the protein that forms spindle microtubules.
Tubulin proteins assemble to form microtubules, including spindle fibers.
Kinetic energy is energy of motion, not the minimum energy needed to initiate a reaction.
Potential energy is stored energy and is not the specific term for initiating a reaction.
Chemical energy is energy stored in chemical bonds, not the threshold required to start a reaction.
Activation energy is the minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction.
46 is not the conventional total ATP yield given for cellular respiration in this curriculum.
40 is not the conventional total ATP yield given for cellular respiration in this curriculum.
The conventional textbook yield for cellular respiration is 38 ATP molecules.
36 is sometimes cited for eukaryotic cells, but the expected textbook answer here is 38.
Ingestion is the taking of food into the body.
Digestion breaks food down into simpler substances rather than taking it in.
Absorption is the passage of digested nutrients into the blood or lymph.
Assimilation is the use of absorbed nutrients by body cells.
Erythrocytes are red blood cells that mainly transport oxygen.
Leukocytes are white blood cells that defend the body against infection and other threats.
Thrombocytes help blood clot rather than serving as the main defence cells.
Albumin is a blood protein, not a cell that performs body defence.
Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from higher to lower concentration.
Filtration is the movement of substances through a barrier due to pressure.
Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy.
Transpiration is water loss from plant surfaces, not this general movement of molecules.
Inhibitors reduce enzyme activity and are not tightly bound organic cofactors.
Activators increase enzyme activity but are not the term for tightly bound organic cofactors.
Coenzymes are organic cofactors, typically loosely bound to enzymes.
A tightly bound organic cofactor is called a prosthetic group.
Meiosis is not generally described in this curriculum as occurring in haploid cells.
Meiosis begins in diploid cells and reduces the chromosome number in the resulting cells.
Triploid cells are not the standard cells in which meiosis occurs in this context.
Tetraploid cells are not the standard answer; the expected starting cells are diploid.
The lungs are part of the respiratory system.
The oral cavity is part of the digestive system and receives food.
The kidneys are part of the urinary system.
The heart is part of the circulatory system.
Glucose is broken down through earlier stages of respiration before its carbon enters the Krebs cycle.
Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl-CoA before its carbon enters the Krebs cycle.
Sucrose must first be broken down into simpler sugars and processed before entering respiration.
Acetyl-CoA combines with oxaloacetate to enter the Krebs cycle.
